text:
Maya: Quick sync — we plan to bring up a customer-facing q4_0 30B model on Dedicated in us-west and eu-west. Goal: ~1k concurrent inference QPS across both regions, p95 latency target <= 700ms. Need recommendations: GPUs (A100/H100/L4), per-GPU concurrency targets, and autoscale headroom. Also kernel preference for this quant profile?

Sam: +1 on headcount planning. couple quick Qs: is 1k QPS peak sustained or spiky? token length distribution?

Maya: Mostly spiky — baseline 300 qps sustained, 1k for ~20-30m during peak. median prompt ~60 tokens, responses ~80 tokens.

bench-bot: Latest synthetic runs (batch=1, seq=140, q4_0):
```
Region  GPU     p50(ms)  p95(ms)  max_qps_per_gpu (est)
us-west A100-80  120      340      45
us-west H100-80  95       270      58
eu-west L4-48    180      520      30
```
Numbers are for single-request concurrency tuning (no prefix cache). Kernel=cutlass by default; triton builds slightly lower p50 on H100 but less stable at high concurrency.

Liam: Based on that, rough math: to hit 1k peak qps with headroom you need ~ (1k / 58) ~= 18 H100s or (1k / 45) ~= 23 A100s. Add autoscale headroom ~25-30% -> plan for 24 H100s or 30 A100s max. For steady 300 qps you need ~6 H100s (300/58=5.2) so min_gpus=6 is reasonable.

Andre: Recommending headroom: set headroom_pct=30 for the Dedicated pools that serve spikes. We saw bursts where cold KV inflate latency; 30% lets autoscaler react without immediate RB. Example config: 
```
autoscale:
  target_qps_per_gpu: 50
  headroom_pct: 30
  min_gpus: 6
  max_gpus: 30
  scale_cooldown_sec: 120
```
This uses target_qps_per_gpu conservative=50 to account for KV and quant overhead.

Nicole: Also consider mixed-GPU pool: put L4s behind lower-cost, lower-latency routes for short prompts only. Route long seq traffic to H100s. Routing policy: latency-first to H100, cost-first to L4 with fallback. Adds complexity but saves committed cost.

Sam: Kernel notes: for q4_0 on H100 we saw best stability with cutlass + kv_shard enabled. Flags to test: `--use-cutlass --kv-sharding --max-concurrency 12` for H100. For A100, `--use-cutlass --max-concurrency 8`. Avoid triton on A100 until we patch kernel OOM at high-concurrency.

Maya: Good call. For rollout plan I propose:
- week 1: canary in us-west with min_gpus=2, max_gpus=10, headroom 30%
- week 2: expand to min_gpus=6, max_gpus=30 in us-west; enable eu-west canary (min=2,max=10)
- monitor p95, error rates, KV hit ratio; rollback if p95 > 900ms or error_rate > 0.5%

Liam: For autoscale policies, also add a secondary metric: tail latency (p95) trigger to scale up immediately, not just QPS. QPS alone misses stalls.

Andre: +1. We should also enable prefix cache priming for common prompts before peak windows (customer sends schedule). Priming reduces actual qps pressure ~10-15%.

Nicole: Cost FYI: 24 H100s reserved vs 30 A100s is material — H100 pool ~20% more expensive per GPU but fewer nodes. Recommend going H100-first for predictable low latency.

Maya: Action items: @Sam can you draft autoscale policy + rollout playbook? @bench-bot can you run a validation bench with kv-cache enabled and post results? I'll schedule canary next Tue.

Sam: on it. I'll push a sample policy and a terraform plan for a 6->24 H100 runway.

bench-bot: K/V cache run scheduled, will post deltas. current expectation: p95 drops ~15% on us-west H100 with cache priming.

Maya: thanks all — leaving this thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
